Jonas/Markus — Greenshore (GS-457) is seeing a rapid rise in 429s and p99 latency from ~08:30 PT. Customer reports queueing/stalls. Alex can share traces. Can you triage and confirm whether this looks like backpressure (queue saturation / concurrency caps) vs. model-side slowdowns?

Immediate goal: reduce user-facing errors and short-term mitigation (rate-limit backoff, route to lower-concurrency pool, temporary capacity bump). Please advise ETA and next steps.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-09-12T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Increased 429s & p99 spikes this morning

Quick update from initial triage — attaching a short set of traces we pulled from the customer tenant.

Findings so far:
- We see request queuing building up on the frontend worker pool; queue depth spikes correlate with p99 spikes.
- Concurrency caps per session are being hit for a subset of long-running calls (median duration within the window is normal, but ~2% of requests are 10x slower).
- Backpressure signals from the runtime are not being propagated to the caller fast enough; requests pile up and then are rejected (429) when the cap is reached.
- No immediate model OOMs or GPU faults in the sampled timeframe.

Short-term actions (in-progress):
1) Enable soft-fail fast-path for queued requests (drops requests earlier with a clear 429 payload + retry-after header) — reduces tail by preventing queue buildup. (10-20m)
2) Temporarily raise concurrency cap for GS-457 on the affected route by 20% while we monitor (5-10m).
3) Route heavy campaigns to the lower-latency pool we've reserved for the account during high load windows. (30m)

Markus is collecting more traces (attached: request_traces_sample.log) and I opened INF-3324. Will confirm when mitigations are live.

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: request_traces_sample.log, text/plain)
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, alex.gupta@greenshore.ai
Cc: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Increased 429s & p99 spikes this morning

Following up with concrete telemetry snapshot — see attached p99_snapshot_20260912.png.

Observations:
- The p50 stays ~120ms; p95 ~430ms; p99 jumps to 2.6s during the 08:30–09:10 window.
- Queue length metric (frontend.request_queue.depth) shows sustained 150–200 requests vs baseline ~12.
- The slow subset of requests are mostly from multi-turn chat sessions where KV cache misses cause longer model generation times.

Mitigations deployed:
- Raised concurrency cap (user-level) by +20% for 15 minutes — observed modest improvement in queue depth.
- Enabled early-reject policy for requests older than 4s with structured retry-after header.
- Created a temporary routing rule to send new campaign traffic to the lighter workload pool (pool-id L-23).

Next: prepare mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf with step-by-step for GS-457 and a proposed configuration change to their session timeouts. I will post a more formal RCA after we stabilize.

— Markus
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: p99_snapshot_20260912.png, image/png)

Team,

Thanks for the quick response. A few asks from leadership:
1) We need a one-page exec brief for the customer and for our leadership chain (timeline, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, risk of recurrence, and next steps + owners). Please have this to me and to Greenshore by EOD PT.
2) Confirm whether a one-hour capacity bump (Dedicated burst or hosted pool) will fully mitigate for the next 24h and what the cost/approval path is.
3) If the root cause is queueing/backpressure, propose a short-term policy change to surface backpressure earlier (e.g., progressive drop thresholds, or faster reject path) and a plan to harden the prefix/KV cache misses that seem implicated.

Jonas/Markus — can you produce the exec brief and proposed approval template for the capacity bump? Vanessa, keep Greenshore in the loop.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Reliability Engineering

Subject: Re: Queued requests causing stalls — exec brief and mitigation

Alex — we pushed a set of mitigations earlier and are monitoring; attaching the exec brief and playbook for immediate steps. High-level:

- Short-term: enabled early-reject with retry-after, temporary +20% concurrency bump, and routing campaign traffic to pool L-23. These lowered queue depth and reduced p99 from 2.6s to ~700ms within 45 minutes.
- Medium-term: we recommend adjusting Greenshore session timeout to 3s for first-pass calls and pinning heavy campaigns to a dedicated pool during burst windows.
- Ask: Would Greenshore be comfortable with a one-hour Dedicated burst (we can fast-approve at $X/hour) so we can fully eliminate residual throttles while we implement cache-hardening and better drop signals?

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook), p99_snapshot_20260912.png (before snapshot).

Next steps / owners:
- Jonas: finalize RCA draft and follow-up JIRA (INF-3324) — due 2026-09-13 10:00 PT.
- Markus: confirm cost and process for a 1hr burst for GS-457 — due 2026-09-12 18:30 PT.
- Vanessa: coordinate customer approval and PO for burst if Greenshore accepts.

Please reply on acceptance for the burst and any questions.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
